newsitem.title: UK: London & Overseas "no comment" on strategic review.
newsitem.headline: London & Overseas "no comment" on strategic review.

text.p: London & Overseas Freighters Plc , the Bermuda-based owner of six tankers, said Monday it had no comment on the progress of its strategic review, now into its sixth month.

In a statement the company said: "The process initiated by the company to explore a range of strategic alternatives aimed at positioning itself to compete more effectively in the changing market for quoted tanker companies is still ongoing and no further comment is appropriate at this time."
London & Overseas announced in February it had embarked on a strategic review.
It was widely read in shipping markets that the Nasdaq-listed firm had effectively put itself up for sale, although there is surprise at the time the process has taken.
Huw Spiers, London & Overseas chief financial officer, told Reuters Monday: "We are still actively in discussions, but there is nothing further I can add at this stage."
Among potential bidders are believed to have been tanker companies Oslo-listed Frontline , the Angelicoussis group, and the Euronav tanker joint venture.
Mike McCarty at US investment bank Gleacher NatWest, which is handling the sale, declined to comment.
London & Overseas said first quarter net income increased to $2.01 million from $0.405 million in the same period a year earlier.
The firm said operating revenues in the three months to the end of June rose to $16.1 million from $14.3 million, helped by the firmer tanker charter market.
